relevance_note: Case report of one woman with three ABCA1 variants and non-classical Tangier disease: 'She was found to have three mutations in the ABCA1 gene.'
method_note: Single case report, read in full by hand; JSON assembled with a short Python script from values chosen while reading; no tables in the paper. In scope: the patient and her sister ('Her sister was also diagnosed with low HDL levels.'), who is an affected relative; the sister was not genotyped (the authors only say 'she might be a carrier'), so she has no variant row. Father (Alzheimer disease) and mother (hypertension) were not tested and are not described as affected by Tangier-related features, so they get no rows. Variant strings are copied with the '>' entity exactly as it appears in the Markdown. Phase of the three variants is not determined: authors 'assume that two mutations are on one allele and one mutation on the other'; zygosity recorded as 'heterozygous' from 'her phenotype and a heterozygous genotype'. Pathogenicity and functional evidence for each variant come partly from the statement naming all three variants ('All three of these mutations have been reported to be deleterious in functional studies'). Lab values not interpreted by the authors were not turned into features: CRP 5.6 mg/L (normal 3.0), fibrinogen 348 mg/dL (normal <340), homocysteine, lipoprotein(a), total cholesterol 60 mg/dL and triglycerides 103 mg/dL. Calculated LDL of 34 mg/dL is described by the authors as 'optimal', not low, so checklist 'low LDL cholesterol' is not reported. 'Diffuse atherosclerosis' does not name non-coronary arteries, so that checklist item is not reported. Tonsil colour unknown ('did not remember if the tonsils were of any unusual color'), so 'orange-colored or enlarged tonsils' is not reported. Abdominal CT without organomegaly is used to exclude hepatomegaly and splenomegaly; lymphadenopathy is left not reported. Year taken from 'Published online: 28 September 2011'. No contradictions found.
